what: Plan 1.41: the generics checked against the text's own words (out/sweep/generic-links.jsonl). A sample of 32: 14 same, 10 part_of, 8 neither.

tally._note: James 2:2 first marked wrong, changed to right by Doug after the Greek was shown: 'I agree on james 2:2 now'

wrong.finding: a habit is not the people; the generic stands for 'some' itself, so no naming word: neither

RIGHT after all (Doug, 2026-10-18: 'I agree on james 2:2 now'): the Greek has no 'man' for him (ἀνήρ is the rich man's); πτωχός stands alone with 'in shabby clothes' attached, as 'the fourth' does in Rev 16:8
same as 'the fourth' (τέταρτος, 16:8): the Greek says 'the fourth' alone, 'angel' is the Berean's; the judge was offered it and reasoned only about 16:5's angel

his_words: do I always need to compare to the one word? the context matters
